  ABSTAIN: None

  City Attorney Bagneris noted the changes resulting from the now
  adopted ordinance will become effective upon publication, with the
  changes to future City Council closed sessions starting at 5:00 p.m. and
  open sessions starting at 6:00 p.m. to begin on a go forward basis,
  starting next week, September 16, 2024.

  Mayor Gordo noted that at next week's City Council meeting, staff will
  provide a report and discussion regarding the recent heat wave
  affecting the City and surrounding region, including power outages,
  responses from Pasadena Water and Power and City departments, as

  Council Minutes  3  09/09/2024
   RECOMMENDATIONS  RECEIVE INFORMATION AND PROVIDE GUIDANCE RELATING
  FROM OFFICERS AND  TO THE CITY'S EFFORTS TO ADDRESS ISSUES ASSOCIATED
  DEPARTMENTS  WITH HOMELESSNESS (Office of the City Manager)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  City Manager
  (1) Receive and provide guidance relating to services provided to the
  unhoused in Pasadena by the City and its governmental and non-
  governmental partners, including guidance relating to Pasadena
  Municipal Code Section 3.24.110(A)(8) which prohibits camping in
  public places, and provide guidance on the City's role, if any, on
  regional efforts to address homelessness.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 30 letters advocating for the City to
  reject homelessness enforcement policies, adopt the "Good Neighbor"
  Pledge, and/or expand housing development and supportive services,
  1 letter expressing safety concerns with homeless encampments in the
  Arroyo Seco, and 10 letters advocating for the City to reaffirm and
  uphold the ordinance prohibiting public camping and obstructing rights
  of way, were received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City
  Council, posted online, and made part of the public record for this item.
  City Manager Marquez provided introductory remarks on the item and
  introduced various City departments that would presenting vital
  information and contributing to discussion on the matter.

  Alexander Hernandez, Assistant to the City Manager, provided
  background information on the item and an overview of the
  presentation. Amanda Cusick, Deputy City Attorney, presented
  background information on the Grants Pass v. Johnson case, the
  Supreme Court's ruling, and the Governor's Executive Order and the
  Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors Action (which both resulted
  from the Supreme Court ruling). Tim Wellman, Chief Assistant City
  Prosecutor, provided an overview of the prosecution process for
  competent unhoused defendants and the Prosecution Division's "care
  first" approach. Bill Huang, Director of Housing, provided an overview
  of government resources, responsibilities, and homeless services.
  Joaquin Siques, Director of Transportation, reported on LA County
  Metro crisis intervention initiatives and homeless outreach partners
  utilized to address homelessness on their transit system. Nathan Press,
  Public Health Program Coordinator, shared success stories of
  homeless individuals that the City has aided, highlighted the multiple
  aspects that contribute to individuals becoming homeless, and reported
  on aspects of the Pasadena Outreach Response Team (PORT)
  services. Jennifer O'Reilly-Jones, Housing Program Coordinator,
  presented demographics of the City's unsheltered population and
  reported on the initiatives of street outreach efforts, housing operations,

Li  and other programs. Tony Zee, representing the PORT Team,
  presented client successes and elaborated on PORT services. Police
  Commander Bill Grisafe reported on the mental health services
  provided by the City's Homeless Outreach Psychiatric Evaluations
  (HOPE) Team. Ted Smith, Assistant City Prosecutor, concluded the
  Council Minutes  4  09/09/2024
   presentation and reported that City Attorney/Prosecutor's Office is
  working on establishing a "Homeless Court" to address issues of
  homelessness and assist unhoused defendants by connecting them to
  interim housing and other services. Members of the staff presentation
  group responded to City Council questions.

  The following individuals expressed concerns pertaining to the
  ineffectiveness of encampment sweeps, expressed opposition to
  criminalizing homelessness, advocated for affordable housing and
  additional resources to address homelessness, and/or provided
  various comments:

  Council Minutes  5  09/09/2024
   Mayor Gordo reported that the San Gabriel Valley Council of
  Government (SGVCOG) has begun discussing how to address the
  matter of homelessness on a regional level, coordinating efforts among
  the 31 associated cities of the SGVCOG, and also reported that he
  extended an invitation to the neighboring cities of Burbank, Glendale,
  and South Pasadena to collaborate with the SGVCOG on the matter.

  Councilmember Lyon thanked City staff for the presentation, and
  members of the public for their comments, hie stated his understanding
  of the Supreme Court's ruling on the Grants Pass case as focused
  specifically on cities' ability to enforce criminal sanctions against
  unhoused individuals for sleeping in public, and whether that violates
  the U.S. Constitution.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding enforcement of
  the City's anti-camping ordinance, City Attorney Bagneris noted that
  enforcement is left to the responding Police Officers' discretion to
  determine if the individual is obstructing a public right-of-way. Chief
  Assistant City Prosecutor Wellman reported that violations of the City's
  ordinance depend on where the individual is sleeping (i.e. municipal
  areas, nonpublic places), and also clarified that the City Prosecutor
  Division would only take enforcement actions if a citation was issued
  by the Police Department. City Attorney Bagneris further clarified that
  the City's anti-camping ordinance does not describe what constitutes
  an obstruction of a sidewalk, and it would be up to responding Police
  Officers to determine the facts in each instance.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding the various
  ways an officer may respond to a situation of an unhoused individual
  sleeping in public, Commander Grisafe stated that responding officers
  may wake up the individual and ask them to move along, issue a
  citation, or connect the individual to PORT or HOPE services. Chief
  Assistant City Prosecutor Wellman reported that the fine for such
  citations is $0 and is primarily used for filing purposes to connect such
  individuals to homeless services. Police Chief Harris also confirmed
  that the City does not place unsheltered individuals on trains, nor send
  them to other cities. He noted that individuals may get off of the train in
  Pasadena and end up staying in the City.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding additional
  recommendations from City staff for Council's consideration, City
  Manager Marquez noted that the importance of the presentation was to
  inform the City Council of the Grants Pass decision, and provide
  context to the challenges and complexity of governing such matters.

  In response to Councilmember Masuda's inquiry regarding Los
L  Angeles County Measure A, Housing Director Huang reported that if
  the Measure passes during the November 2024 election, it will
  essentially ensure continuation of funding for homeless services and
  provide additional funds for capital development to build more housing.

  Council Minutes  6  09/09/2024
   In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding motel vouchers
  and receiving additional services, Housing Director Huang reported that
  once an unhoused individual receives a voucher, they temporarily
  obtain a safe and set location that allows them to be connected to
  supportive services, as well as potentially accessing permanent
  housing. Councilmember Jones advocated for increased funding to
  expand the PORT team.

  Discussion ensued regarding funding for outreach services, ongoing
  permanent supportive housing projects, interim housing projects,
  staffing challenges, continued collaboration with the County of Los
  Angeles, and expansion of the PORT team.

  In response to Councilmember Rivas' inquiry regarding enforcement of
  the City's after-hours park ordinance, Commander Grisafe reported that
  after 10:00 p.m., Park Safety Specialists will have the public vacate the
  park. He noted that they may issue warnings or citations to those who
  do not leave, when necessary. He also noted that similar to
  enforcement of the anti-camping ordinance, citations are then filed with
  the City Prosecutor's Division and unhoused individuals are connected
  to homeless services.

  In response to Councilmember Rivas' inquiry regarding what further
  enforcement would mean for homeless services providers,
  representatives from Union Station Homeless Services, Door of Hope,
  and Friends-ln-Deed emphasized that further criminalization of
  unhoused individuals could increase trauma, lead to distrust of law
  enforcement, and hinder progress made by outreach service workers.
  Councilmember Williams expressed support for the Homeless Court
  program, to connect unhoused individuals with services that they need,
  and also supported a "care first" enforcement approach.

  Vice Mayor Madison expressed concerns regarding the duality of the
  homelessness crisis, noting that businesses that close due to direct
  impacts of the homelessness crisis, would cause resulting economic
  activity to decline, and consequently impact City resources to fund
  homeless services. He advocated for more permanent supportive
  housing, having additional safety personnel at the Metro Light Rail
  stops within the City, and funding and implementing a fourth HOPE
  team to increase homeless outreach sen/ices.

  City Attorney Bagneris reported on the process to establish a Homeless
  Court program, noting that the Los Angeles County Superior
  Courthouse in Pasadena is supportive of allowing the City to utilize
  courtrooms, but stated that funding and sen/ices would come from the
  City.

Council Minutes  7  09/09/2024
   Councilmember Hampton expressed his support for a Homeless Court
  program, and suggested that the item be further discussed by the
  Public Safety Committee.
